vehicle.name: 2002 Pontiac Grand Prix GTP 3.8 supercharged
vehicle.notes: OBD-II. The diagnostic plug is under the dash on the driver's side.

connection.notes: GM used J1850 VPW in this era (the service manual refers to 'Class 2'). Many cheap ELM327 clones don't support VPW; use an adapter that lists it, such as the OBDLink SX.

rpm_warm_idle.label: Warm idle speed
rpm_warm_idle.condition: warm idle in Park, A/C off
rpm_warm_idle.note: No published idle spec for the GTP was found. The PCM controls idle with the IAC valve; a steady idle in this range is typical for the 3800. A non-supercharged 2002 GT was logged at about 900 rpm.

coolant_warm.label: Coolant, warm
coolant_warm.note: 195 F thermostat. Owners report the PCM turns the low-speed fan on around 215 F and high speed around 226-228 F (one cites the factory manual at 221 F for high speed).

maf_idle.label: Mass air flow at idle
maf_idle.condition: warm idle in Park, A/C off
maf_idle.note: A healthy L67 reads about 4-6 g/s at warm idle (one healthy car: 4.7 g/s), rising with RPM.

ltft.label: Long-term fuel trim
ltft.note: Owners treat about +/-5% as normal. Persistent -15 to -25% shows up on L67s with vacuum leaks, injector or tune problems; large positive trims at idle point to vacuum leaks. Watch/problem limits are the app's.

stft.label: Short-term fuel trim
stft.note: Short-term trim moves quickly; about +/-10% is considered acceptable.

o2_upstream.label: Upstream O2
o2_upstream.note: Narrowband sensor: switches between about 0.1 and 0.9 V several times a second when warm.

o2_downstream.label: Downstream O2 (after catalyst)
o2_downstream.note: With a working catalyst the downstream sensor stays fairly steady; if it switches like the upstream one, the catalyst is weak.

battery_running.label: Charging voltage
battery_running.note: General automotive charging range. One owner's idle surge and stalling went away after the battery was charged.

fuel_pressure.label: Fuel pressure (gauge, not in OBD data)
fuel_pressure.note: Series II L67: 48-55 psi with the pump running (a factory manual quote gives 48-54). Above 55 psi can cause rich running; don't exceed 65 psi. Lower with vacuum on the regulator. Measure with a gauge on the fuel rail.

known_issues.title: Intake gasket and PCV vacuum leaks
known_issues.symptoms: High or rough idle, idle surge; lean codes P0171/P0174, misfire P0300.
known_issues.what_data_shows: Positive fuel trims at idle that come back toward 0 at 2500 rpm.
known_issues.checks: Listen for hissing; spray carb cleaner around the upper intake and PCV hoses with the engine idling and watch for an RPM change. Upper/lower intake gaskets can also leak coolant into the oil.

known_issues.title: Supercharger coupler rattle
known_issues.symptoms: A rattle like rocks tumbling at idle that goes away with throttle.
known_issues.checks: The coupler between the supercharger pulley shaft and rotors wears; replacing it usually fixes the noise (reported on a 1997 GTP).

known_issues.title: Idle surge or stalling with a weak battery
known_issues.symptoms: Idle surges or the engine stalls at idle.
known_issues.checks: Charge and test the battery and check the charging system before replacing sensors (an owner who had replaced the MAF, MAP and IAC fixed it this way).

known_issues.title: Cheap OBD adapters won't connect
known_issues.symptoms: Scanner can't talk to the car.
known_issues.checks: Use an adapter that supports J1850 VPW (GM Class 2), such as an OBDLink SX; many cheap ELM327 clones don't.

research.notes: No factory scan-data specs for idle RPM, MAF or trims were reachable; those come from owner reports. GM enhanced (mode 22) PIDs for this car are not included yet: they need a source that gives each PID and its formula.
